adjudicator: eval-category wave lane N2 (one adjudicator, an AI agent; not an independent human review)
source: eval/data/gold/contradictions.json (generated by eval/generators/amara-life-gen.ts; that file is not hand-edited, so relabels live here)
corpus: eval/data/amara-life-v1 (inspected while adjudicating, so it is development data, never a holdout)
rules: contradiction: the two sides state different values for the same fact about the same entity, for overlapping times, and neither the wording nor the elapsed time explains the difference

temporal_evolution: the later side's wording (now, since we last discussed, effective, formally approved) or the dates show the value or plan changed over time; a plan replaced by a decision counts here
temporal_supersession: the newer claim replaces the older one (the stale_facts section)
holder_difference: the sides are different holders' targets or preferences, not one fact
not_same_fact: the sides name different entities or different facts, so they cannot contradict
claim_present: exact when the gold claim string occurs verbatim in the source text; paraphrase when the same meaning occurs in different words or with link markup; absent otherwise
Labels are never deleted: every pair keeps its row, and the N2 runner scores the judge against both the original and the adjudicated label

pairs.rationale: Both sides recall the size of the same past funding round (a fixed historical fact) five days apart with different amounts.
pairs.canonical_note: The gold reason says the email quotes the term sheet directly, but the email says 'if I remember correctly'; the canonical side is undetermined.

pairs.rationale: The email names one company (an 'AI' name and link) and the note names a differently named 'Analytics' company, so the text does not establish one entity. If they were the same entity the email's 'grown to 45' ten days after 'about 60' would itself be inconsistent.
The email names the lead investor of the company's Series A; the note names the lead investor of its Series B. Different rounds are different facts.
Both sides state the founder's equity after the same Series A dilution, three weeks apart, with no intervening event: 17% versus 15%.

The meeting reports the company's own target round size; the earlier note says 'we're targeting a $25M Series B' in the investor's voice ('positions us well for meaningful ownership'). These read as two holders' targets a month apart, not one fact.

pairs.rationale: The later meeting says the burn multiple 'is sitting at 1.8 right now ... down from where they were six months ago', i.e. it describes an improving trend; the note five weeks earlier says 2.4. Consistent with change over time.

claim_present.source_b: paraphrase (link markup splits the name from 'takes the Helios board seat')

pairs.rationale: The February note records a tentative plan; the April meeting records the board formally approving a different appointment. The gold reason itself says the note reflects an earlier tentative plan.
22 months versus about 14 months of runway, 17 days apart; elapsed time cannot explain an eight-month gap.

The note says the company is 'holding firm at a $30M cap'; five weeks later the email says it is 'still looking to close out the SAFE at a $45M cap'. 'Still' presents one ongoing negotiation, so the caps conflict, although a renegotiation in between is possible.
pairs.canonical_note: The gold reason says the email quotes the signed SAFE, but the email says the SAFE is not yet closed; the canonical side is undetermined.
